## TypeSafe: VERIFIED by a real call

- `POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone`, header `Authorization: Bearer $TYPESAFE_API_KEY`, `Content-Type: application/json`
- Request body (several Nouls = several keys under `questions`; they run in parallel; the keys are yours to name):
```json
{
  "model": "jev-latest",
  "state": {
    "offer": {
      "price": 58,
      "terms_text": "$58/mo for 3 months, then $95/mo"
    }
  },
  "questions": {
    "raises_price_after_intro": {
      "type": "noul",
      "instructions": "Does `offer` raise the price after an introductory period?"
    }
  }
}
```
- Probability for question `<id>` is `answers.<id>.noul`, a number from 0 to 1 (chance of yes).
- Model name `jev-latest` is from the docs; `GET /v1/models` lists others (docs only, not verified).

- Verified response top-level keys: ['answers', 'model', 'usage']; answer keys: ['noul', 'type']

## Senso context search: VERIFIED by a real call

- `POST {SENSO_BASE_URL}/org/search/context`, header `X-API-Key: $SENSO_API_KEY`. Default base `https://apiv2.senso.ai/api/v1`.
- Request body (`query` required; `max_results` default 5, max 20; `search_type` hybrid|lexical|vector):
```json
{
  "query": "introductory rate reverts to standard price",
  "max_results": 3,
  "search_type": "hybrid"
}
```
- Results are under `results`, each with `content_id`, `version_id`, `chunk_text`, `score`, `rank` (docs; the keys seen in the real call are listed below).

- Verified response top-level keys: ['max_results', 'query', 'results', 'search_type', 'total_results']; result keys: ['chunk_index', 'chunk_text', 'content_chunk_id', 'content_id', 'content_type', 'inclusion_reason', 'kb_node_id', 'rank', 'retrieval', 'score', 'source_type', 'title', 'vector_id', 'version_id']

## Also verified (P5 run against the real APIs, 2026-11-20)

- TypeSafe accepts several Nouls in ONE request (three keys under `questions`), and `state` can hold a list such as `plan_terms: [chunk_text, ...]`. Model `jev-latest` worked.
- Senso `/org/search/context` with `max_results: 3` returns up to 3 chunks per query; the same `content_id` can appear more than once (different chunks of one document).
- Trap offer ("$58/mo for 3 months, then $95, 24-month contract") came back p = 0.98 / 0.71 / 0.96, so `reject`. Clean offer ("$58/mo fixed 12 months, no added fees") came back p = 0.02 / 0.03 / 0.01, so `pass`.
